Summary
Jack writes to his friends or family about the end of the war and the anticipation of returning home. He mentions spending too much time listening to the news and not having the peace of mind to write. He expresses hope that soon it will be their turn to celebrate and return home. The letter also mentions waiting for the Japanese representatives and the War Department plans for demobilization. The tone is hopeful and reflective.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_42a) --- Dear Folks: It has been quite some time now since I last wrote to you. I suppose you know the reason why. A lot of things have happened. The most important of all things. We were spending too much time listening to the news. I did not have the peace of mind to sit down and write a letter. all that is left now is the hope that it will soon be our turn --- Page 2 (Beckerman_42b) --- To have always celebrating but they have gone We heard a new broadcast of the celebratin we are New York City and It are each other Aug we many days will be coming home and new lucky now we be changed you to what you we see now your we don't know anything --- Page 3 (Beckerman_42c) --- We have heard about that present time. [illegible] the war is over, and that is the most important thing. At least you know there is nothing to worry about. Everybody is very restless here and all you hear concerns going home. Nothing else is talked about. At present we are waiting for the Jap representatives. [illegible] Manila. --- Page 4 (Beckerman_42d) --- + to officially sign the surrender terms. We knew the war was coming to a close for some time before the announce- ment. And now we are waiting for The War Department plans for demobilization. I wish I could be with you celebrating the wonderful occasion. I hope it will not be too long. Love Jack
